question:
Read the following passage and answer the questions based on the passage:

The idea of progress has always gone hand in hand with the evolution of human beings and the invention of technology. Each technological revolution has unearthed revolutionary changes that have rewritten the human experience in the past. From the invention of the printing press to the invention of the internet, technological breakthroughs have shaped the manner in which we live, work, and communicate. But with our arrival in an age of artificial intelligence, automation, and biotechnology comes a growing paradox: while these technologies offer unparalleled convenience and power, they also undermine tried-and-true social forms and erode the very notion of what it means to be human. Technological advances, first of all, have provided standards of living much better. Medical advances like gene editing and precision medicine hold the promise to cure diseases that were once thought incurable. Communication technology has made the world think alike in ways that people could not have imagined a couple of decades ago, with people able to work together across borders and cultures with relative ease. But the same technology has profound implications. Automation is taking away jobs for millions of people, particularly where human labour can be automated. The speed of innovation has left millions behind, and with it there is a feeling of disconnection, fear for the future. Secondly, our dependence on technology is creating basic questions regarding privacy, security, and freedom. As we introduce AI into everyday life, do we have to sit back and ask ourselves: are we Master of Technology, or is technology the master of us? The paradox of progress, then, is in its double-edged nature. On one hand, technology comes bearing answers to some of humankind’s biggest problems, yet it also brings new issues that human beings must resolve in order to make progress mean a more just and sustainable tomorrow.

 

What is the main paradox introduced in the passage regarding technological advancements?
option_1: Technology always improves the quality of life
option_2: Technology eliminates all forms of labor
option_3: Technology offers convenience but also undermines social structures and the notion of being human
option_4: Technology solves all human problems without consequences
solution_text:
The correct answer is 'Technology offers convenience but also undermines social structures and the notion of being human'.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage states: “But with our arrival in an age of artificial intelligence, automation, and biotechnology comes a growing paradox: while these technologies offer unparalleled convenience and power, they also undermine tried-and-true social forms and erode the very notion of what it means to be human.”

• This is reinforced elsewhere: “The idea of progress has always gone hand in hand with the evolution of human beings and the invention of technology.”

• This directly supports ‘Technology offers convenience but also undermines social structures and the notion of being human’ as the answer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Detail and inference questions in Reading Comprehension are answered by locating the exact supporting line in the passage rather than by outside knowledge, even when an option sounds generally true.

 

NOTE

• The other options either reverse the passage's stated relationship, introduce a detail the passage does not mention, or describe a related but distinct idea from what the question actually asks.

question:
Read the following passage and answer the questions based on the passage:

Movies, being a potent medium of storytelling, have a tremendous influence on society, determining cultural norms, public opinion, and individual opinions. Films are more than a form of entertainment; they represent and caricature social values and are a mirror to the collective consciousness of society. Movies can introduce new ideas, challenge old prejudices, and initiate serious discussions on social issues. Legendary characters and stories can touch the hearts of generations, defining fashion, vocabulary, and even ambition. The pictorial and emotional power of film provides a special kind of empathy, taking viewers into other worlds and experiences, hence understanding and expanding horizons. Still, this power has responsibility; movies can reinforce stereotypes, help spread harmful ideologies, or offer unrealized versions of life, and all the more reason to embrace critical interaction with the narratives we watch.

 

What is one of the major influences of movies on society according to the text?
option_1: They only entertain and do not impact societal values
option_2: They determine cultural norms, public opinion, and individual opinions
option_3: They are used primarily for advertising products
option_4: They focus solely on fantasy and escapism
solution_text:
The correct answer is 'They determine cultural norms, public opinion, and individual opinions'.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage states: “Movies, being a potent medium of storytelling, have a tremendous influence on society, determining cultural norms, public opinion, and individual opinions.”

• This is reinforced elsewhere: “Films are more than a form of entertainment; they represent and caricature social values and are a mirror to the collective consciousness of society.”

• This directly supports ‘They determine cultural norms, public opinion, and individual opinions’ as the answer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.
